anchor_comparisons: The positive anchor's 14.28-16.38 band is broadly comparable because current issuer facts include customer demand, purchase orders, completed multi-year arrangements and sold-out HBM4 production capacity.

The counter anchor's 7.77-9.87 band understates current order visibility, though its caution is useful because customer-level quantities, pricing, termination terms and shipment conversion remain undisclosed.
disagreements: I place more weight than the memo midpoint on issuer-stated purchase orders and completed mid-to-long-term customer arrangements.
I assign no contract or qualification weight to the customer-official technology introduction by itself.
payload.rationale: Customer demand for planned production, purchase orders against prepared capacity, completed mid-to-long-term arrangements and sold-out HBM4 production capacity create a stronger visibility plane than non-binding demand indications. Multi-year contract language supports duration, while the customer-official technology reference corroborates participation but is not treated as an order. The case remains below the top band because contract economics and actual shipment conversion are not disclosed.
payload.why_not_higher: A higher value requires customer-specific committed quantities, minimum-purchase and cancellation terms, price-reset mechanics and evidence that orders converted to shipment and cash without customer schedule delay.
payload.why_not_lower: A lower value would ignore the combination of purchase orders, sold-out planned capacity and completed longer-duration customer arrangements, which is materially stronger than generic demand commentary.
